body.en: This chapter covers two closely related ideas AIST Math 2 tests together: building new functions from old ones (composition, inverses), and solving equation types that go beyond linear/quadratic — rational, polynomial, exponential, and logarithmic.
body.ar: This chapter covers two closely related ideas AIST Math 2 tests together: building new الدوال from old ones (composition, inverses), and solving المعادلة types that go beyond linear/quadratic — rational, كثيرة الحدود, exponential, and logarithmic.

body.en: The composition of \( f \) and \( g \), written \( (f\circ g)(x) \) or \( f(g(x)) \), means: apply \( g \) first, then apply \( f \) to the result. In general \( f(g(x))\neq g(f(x)) \) — order matters.

body.en:
Let \( f(x)=2x+3 \) and \( g(x)=x^2-1 \). Find \( f(g(2)) \) and \( g(f(1)) \).

\[ g(2)=2^2-1=3, \qquad f(g(2))=f(3)=2(3)+3=9. \]

\[ f(1)=2(1)+3=5, \qquad g(f(1))=g(5)=5^2-1=24. \]

Different order, different answer — exactly as the definition warns.
body.ar:

\[ f(1)=2(1)+3=5, \qquad g(f(1))=g(5)=5^2-1=24. \]

Different order, different الإجابة — exactly as the definition warns.

body.en: A function \( f \) is one-to-one if it never sends two different inputs to the same output. Only one-to-one functions have an inverse \( f^{-1} \), the function that undoes \( f \): \[ f\big(f^{-1}(x)\big)=x \quad\text{and}\quad f^{-1}\big(f(x)\big)=x. \] To find \( f^{-1} \) algebraically: write \( y=f(x) \), swap \( x \) and \( y \), then solve for \( y \).
body.ar: A الدالة \( f \) is one-to-one if it never sends two different inputs to the same output. Only one-to-one الدوال have an inverse \( f^{-1} \), the الدالة that undoes \( f \): \[ f\big(f^{-1}(x)\big)=x \quad\text{and}\quad f^{-1}\big(f(x)\big)=x. \] To find \( f^{-1} \) algebraically: write \( y=f(x) \), swap \( x \) and \( y \), then أوجد قيمة \( y \).

label.en: Worked example 4.B — Find and verify an inverse
label.ar: مثال محلول 4.B — Find and verify an inverse

body.en:
Find \( f^{-1}(x) \) for \( f(x)=2x+3 \), and check it.

Write \( y=2x+3 \); swap: \( x=2y+3 \); solve: \( y=\dfrac{x-3}{2} \). So \( f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{x-3}{2} \).

Check at \( x=7 \): \( f^{-1}(7)=\dfrac{7-3}{2}=2 \), and \( f(2)=2(2)+3=7 \) ✓ — back where we started.
body.ar:
Find \( f^{-1}(x) \) for \( f(x)=2x+3 \), and check it.

Write \( y=2x+3 \); swap: \( x=2y+3 \); solve: \( y=\dfrac{x-3}{2} \). So \( f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{x-3}{2} \).

Check at \( x=7 \): \( f^{-1}(7)=\dfrac{7-3}{2}=2 \), and \( f(2)=2(2)+3=7 \) ✓ — back حيث we started.

body.en: A rational equation has a variable in a denominator. Solve by clearing denominators (multiply both sides by them), then solve the resulting polynomial equation — but always check each solution in the original equation, since a value that makes a denominator zero is an extraneous solution and must be rejected even if it satisfies the cleared version.
body.ar: A rational equation has a المتغير in a denominator. Solve by clearing denominators (multiply both sides by them), then solve the resulting كثيرة الحدود المعادلة — but always check each الحل in the original المعادلة, since a value that makes a denominator zero is an extraneous solution and must be rejected even if it satisfies the cleared version.

label.en: Worked example 4.C — Solve a rational equation
label.ar: مثال محلول 4.C — Solve a rational المعادلة

body.en:
Solve \( \dfrac{x+1}{x-2}=3 \) (note \( x\neq2 \)).

Multiply both sides by \( x-2 \): \( x+1=3(x-2)=3x-6 \). So \( 7=2x \), \( x=\dfrac{7}{2} \). Since \( \tfrac72\neq2 \), it's valid. Check: \( \dfrac{\tfrac72+1}{\tfrac72-2}=\dfrac{\tfrac92}{\tfrac32}=3 \) ✓.
body.ar:
الشرح الرياضي (الدوال والمعادلات المتقدمة):

Solve \( \dfrac{x+1}{x-2}=3 \) (note \( x\neq2 \)).

Multiply both sides by \( x-2 \): \( x+1=3(x-2)=3x-6 \). So \( 7=2x \), \( x=\dfrac{7}{2} \). Since \( \tfrac72\neq2 \), it's valid. Check: \( \dfrac{\tfrac72+1}{\tfrac72-2}=\dfrac{\tfrac92}{\tfrac32}=3 \) ✓.

body.en: For a polynomial \( f(x) \) and a number \( c \): \[ f(c)=0 \quad\iff\quad (x-c)\text{ is a factor of }f(x). \]
body.ar: For a كثيرة الحدود \( f(x) \) and a number \( c \): \[ f(c)=0 \quad\iff\quad (x-c)\text{ is a factor of }f(x). \]

body.en:
(\( \Leftarrow \)) If \( (x-c) \) is a factor, then \( f(x)=(x-c)q(x) \) for some polynomial \( q \), so \( f(c)=(c-c)q(c)=0 \).

(\( \Rightarrow \)) Polynomial division always lets us write \( f(x)=(x-c)q(x)+r \) for some constant remainder \( r \) (dividing by a linear factor leaves a constant remainder). Evaluate at \( x=c \): \( f(c)=(c-c)q(c)+r=0+r=r \). So if \( f(c)=0 \), then \( r=0 \), which means \( f(x)=(x-c)q(x) \) exactly — \( (x-c) \) is a factor. \( \blacksquare \)
body.ar:
(\( \Leftarrow \)) If \( (x-c) \) is a factor, then \( f(x)=(x-c)q(x) \) for some كثيرة الحدود \( q \), so \( f(c)=(c-c)q(c)=0 \).

(\( \Rightarrow \)) كثيرة الحدود division always lets us write \( f(x)=(x-c)q(x)+r \) for some الثابت remainder \( r \) (dividing by a linear factor leaves a الثابت remainder). احسب قيمة at \( x=c \): \( f(c)=(c-c)q(c)+r=0+r=r \). So if \( f(c)=0 \), then \( r=0 \), which means \( f(x)=(x-c)q(x) \) exactly — \( (x-c) \) is a factor. \( \blacksquare \)

body.en:
Factor \( f(x)=x^3-4x^2+x+6 \) completely.

Test small integer candidates: \( f(-1)=(-1)^3-4(1)+(-1)+6=-1-4-1+6=0 \). By Theorem 4.1, \( (x+1) \) is a factor. Dividing gives \( f(x)=(x+1)(x^2-5x+6) \), and the quadratic factors further: \( x^2-5x+6=(x-2)(x-3) \). So

\[ f(x)=(x+1)(x-2)(x-3). \]

Check: expanding \( (x+1)(x-2)(x-3) \) does give back \( x^3-4x^2+x+6 \), and indeed \( f(2)=8-16+2+6=0 \) and \( f(3)=27-36+3+6=0 \) confirm the other two roots.
body.ar:

\[ f(x)=(x+1)(x-2)(x-3). \]

Check: expanding \( (x+1)(x-2)(x-3) \) does give back \( x^3-4x^2+x+6 \), and indeed \( f(2)=8-16+2+6=0 \) and \( f(3)=27-36+3+6=0 \) confirm the other two roots.

body.en: An exponential equation has the variable in an exponent; solve by matching bases (\( b^{m}=b^{n}\Rightarrow m=n \)) when possible. A logarithmic equation has the variable inside a log; the key identity is \( \log_b x+\log_b y=\log_b(xy) \), and every solution must be checked against the log's domain (\( x>0 \)).
body.ar: An exponential equation has the المتغير in an exponent; solve by matching bases (\( b^{m}=b^{n}\Rightarrow m=n \)) عندما possible. A logarithmic equation has the المتغير inside a log; the key المتطابقة is \( \log_b x+\log_b y=\log_b(xy) \), and every الحل must be checked against the log's المجال (\( x>0 \)).

label.en: Worked example 4.E — Solve an exponential equation
label.ar: مثال محلول 4.E — Solve an exponential المعادلة

body.ar:
الشرح الرياضي (الدوال والمعادلات المتقدمة):

Solve \( 2^{x+1}=32 \).

Write \( 32=2^5 \), so \( 2^{x+1}=2^5 \). Matching exponents: \( x+1=5 \), so \( x=4 \).

label.en: Worked example 4.F — Solve a logarithmic equation, checking domain
label.ar: مثال محلول 4.F — Solve a logarithmic المعادلة, checking المجال

body.en:
Solve \( \log_2 x+\log_2(x-2)=3 \).

Combine: \( \log_2\big(x(x-2)\big)=3 \), so \( x(x-2)=2^3=8 \), i.e. \( x^2-2x-8=0 \), which factors as \( (x-4)(x+2)=0 \), giving \( x=4 \) or \( x=-2 \).

Check domain: \( \log_2 x \) requires \( x>0 \), so \( x=-2 \) is rejected (extraneous). Only \( x=4 \) is valid — check: \( \log_2 4+\log_2 2=2+1=3 \) ✓.
body.ar:
Solve \( \log_2 x+\log_2(x-2)=3 \).

Combine: \( \log_2\big(x(x-2)\big)=3 \), so \( x(x-2)=2^3=8 \), i.e. \( x^2-2x-8=0 \), which factors as \( (x-4)(x+2)=0 \), giving \( x=4 \) or \( x=-2 \).

Check المجال: \( \log_2 x \) requires \( x>0 \), so \( x=-2 \) is rejected (extraneous). Only \( x=4 \) is valid — check: \( \log_2 4+\log_2 2=2+1=3 \) ✓.

body.en:
Extraneous Solutions: Multiplying rational equations by clearing denominators can introduce false roots where the original denominator is zero. Always check candidates in the original expression.

Logarithm Domain Violation: In \(\log_b(g(x))\), the argument must satisfy \(g(x) > 0\). Never test roots in combined log forms (like \(\log(x^2)\)); you must test them in the original separate logs.

Composition Order: \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\) is generally not equal to \((g \circ f)(x) = g(f(x))\). Also remember that the domain of \(f \circ g\) requires \(x \in \operatorname{dom}(g)\) and \(g(x) \in \operatorname{dom}(f)\).
body.ar:
Extraneous الحلول: Multiplying rational المعادلات by clearing denominators can introduce false roots حيث the original denominator is zero. Always check candidates in the original العبارة الجبرية.

Logarithm المجال Violation: In \(\log_b(g(x))\), the argument must satisfy \(g(x) > 0\). Never test roots in combined log forms (like \(\log(x^2)\)); you must test them in the original separate logs.

Composition Order: \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\) is generally not equal to \((g \circ f)(x) = g(f(x))\). Also remember that the المجال of \(f \circ g\) requires \(x \in \operatorname{dom}(g)\) and \(g(x) \in \operatorname{dom}(f)\).

question.en: Solve the rational equation for all real values of \( x \): \[ \frac{x}{x-2} + \frac{1}{x-4} = \frac{2}{(x-2)(x-4)} \]
question.ar: حل the rational equation for all real values of \( x \): \[ \frac{x}{x-2} + \frac{1}{x-4} = \frac{2}{(x-2)(x-4)} \]

solution.en:
Step 1: Identify domain restrictions:
Denominators cannot be zero: \( x eq 2 \) and \( x eq 4 \).

Step 2: Clear denominators by multiplying by \( (x-2)(x-4) \):
\[ x(x-4) + (x-2) = 2 \] \[ x^2 - 4x + x - 2 = 2 \implies x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0. \]

Step 3: Factor the quadratic equation:
\[ (x - 4)(x + 1) = 0 \implies x = 4 \quad\text{or}\quad x = -1. \]

Step 4: Check for extraneous solutions:
\( x = 4 \) violates the domain restriction \( x eq 4 \) (it produces division by zero), and must be rejected.
\( x = -1 \) is valid: \[ \frac{-1}{-3} + \frac{1}{-5} = \frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{5} = \frac{2}{15}, \qquad \frac{2}{(-3)(-5)} = \frac{2}{15} \quad \checkmark. \]
Thus the unique real solution is \( \mathbf{x = -1} \).

question.en:
Consider the function \( f(x) = \sqrt{2x - 5} + 3 \).
(a) Find the domain and range of \( f(x) \).
(b) Find the explicit equation for the inverse function \( f^{-1}(x) \), including its restricted domain.
question.ar:
Consider the function \( f(x) = \sqrt{2x - 5} + 3 \).
(a) أوجد domain and range of \( f(x) \).
(b) أوجد explicit equation for the inverse function \( f^{-1}(x) \), including its restricted domain.

solution.en:
Part (a): Domain and Range of \( f \):
1. Radicand non-negative: \( 2x - 5 \geq 0 \implies 2x \geq 5 \implies \mathbf{\operatorname{dom}(f) = \left[\frac{5}{2}, \infty\right)} \).
2. Since \( \sqrt{2x - 5} \geq 0 \), \( f(x) = \sqrt{2x - 5} + 3 \geq 3 \implies \mathbf{\operatorname{range}(f) = [3, \infty)} \).

Part (b): Derive \( f^{-1}(x) \):
1. Set \( y = \sqrt{2x - 5} + 3 \) and swap \( x \) and \( y \):
\[ x = \sqrt{2y - 5} + 3 \]
2. Isolate the square root:
\[ x - 3 = \sqrt{2y - 5} \]
3. Square both sides (valid for \( x \geq 3 \)):
\[ (x - 3)^2 = 2y - 5 \implies 2y = (x - 3)^2 + 5 \implies y = \frac{(x - 3)^2 + 5}{2}. \]
4. State the inverse with domain:
\[ \mathbf{f^{-1}(x) = \frac{x^2 - 6x + 14}{2}, \quad x \geq 3.} \]
solution.ar:
Part (a): Domain and Range of \( f \):

2. Since \( \sqrt{2x - 5} \geq 0 \), \( f(x) = \sqrt{2x - 5} + 3 \geq 3 \implies \mathbf{\operatorname{range}(f) = [3, \infty)} \).

Part (b): Derive \( f^{-1}(x) \):

\[ x = \sqrt{2y - 5} + 3 \]
2. Isolate the square root:

3. ربّع الطرفين (valid for \( x \geq 3 \)):
\[ (x - 3)^2 = 2y - 5 \implies 2y = (x - 3)^2 + 5 \implies y = \frac{(x - 3)^2 + 5}{2}. \]
4. State the inverse with domain:
\[ \mathbf{f^{-1}(x) = \frac{x^2 - 6x + 14}{2}, \quad x \geq 3.} \]

question.en:
The polynomial \( P(x) = 2x^3 + kx^2 - 7x + 6 \) has \( (x - 2) \) as a factor.
(a) Find the value of \( k \).
(b) Factor \( P(x) \) completely over the real numbers and list all its roots.
question.ar:
The polynomial \( P(x) = 2x^3 + kx^2 - 7x + 6 \) has \( (x - 2) \) as a حلّل.
(a) أوجد قيمة \( k \).
(b) حلّل \( P(x) \) compليكنely over the real numbers and list all its roots.

solution.en:
Part (a): Find \( k \) via the Factor Theorem:
By Theorem 4.1, \( (x - 2) \) is a factor if and only if \( P(2) = 0 \):
\[ P(2) = 2(2)^3 + k(2)^2 - 7(2) + 6 = 0 \] \[ 2(8) + 4k - 14 + 6 = 16 + 4k - 8 = 4k + 8 = 0 \implies 4k = -8 \implies \mathbf{k = -2}. \]

Part (b): Divide and factor completely:
Polynomial division of \( 2x^3 - 2x^2 - 7x + 6 \) by \( x - 2 \):
\[ 2x^3 - 2x^2 - 7x + 6 = (x - 2)(2x^2 + 2x - 3). \]
Solve \( 2x^2 + 2x - 3 = 0 \) using the quadratic formula:
\[ x = \frac{-2 \pm \sqrt{2^2 - 4(2)(-3)}}{2(2)} = \frac{-2 \pm \sqrt{4 + 24}}{4} = \frac{-2 \pm \sqrt{28}}{4} = \frac{-2 \pm 2\sqrt{7}}{4} = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{7}}{2}. \]
Factored form: \[ \mathbf{P(x) = (x - 2)\left(2x^2 + 2x - 3\right)} \]
Roots: \( \mathbf{x = 2, \quad x = \frac{-1 + \sqrt{7}}{2}, \quad x = \frac{-1 - \sqrt{7}}{2}.} \)

question.en: Solve the logarithmic equation for \( x \): \[ \log_3(x + 2) + \log_3(x - 4) = 3 \]
question.ar: حل the logarithmic equation for \( x \): \[ \log_3(x + 2) + \log_3(x - 4) = 3 \]

solution.en:
Step 1: Determine domain restrictions:
\( x + 2 > 0 \implies x > -2 \) and \( x - 4 > 0 \implies x > 4 \).
Both hold simultaneously when \( \mathbf{x > 4} \).

Step 2: Combine logarithms using the product property:
\[ \log_3\big((x + 2)(x - 4)\big) = 3 \]

Step 3: Convert to exponential form:
\[ (x + 2)(x - 4) = 3^3 = 27 \] \[ x^2 - 2x - 8 = 27 \implies x^2 - 2x - 35 = 0. \]

Step 4: Factor the quadratic:
\[ (x - 7)(x + 5) = 0 \implies x = 7 \quad\text{or}\quad x = -5. \]

Step 5: Apply domain check:
\( x = -5 \) produces \( \log_3(-3) \), which is undefined in real numbers (extraneous).
\( x = 7 \) satisfies \( x > 4 \):
Check: \( \log_3(9) + \log_3(3) = 2 + 1 = 3 \) ✓.
Therefore, the unique solution is \( \mathbf{x = 7} \).

question.en:
The graph of the function \( f(x) = (x - 1)^2 - 4 \) is shown in the standard \((x, y)\) coordinate plane below.

What is the range of \( f \)?
question.ar:
حل المسألة التالية في (Advanced Functions & Equations): The graph of the function \( f(x) = (x - 1)^2 - 4 \) is shown in the standard \((x, y)\) coordinate plane below.

What is the range of \( f \)?

hints.en: Identify the vertex and direction of opening: The function \( f(x) = (x - 1)^2 - 4 \) is written in vertex form, \( f(x) = a(x - h)^2 + k \), where \( a = 1 \), \( h = 1 \), and \( k = -4 \). The vertex of the parabola is at \((1, -4)\).

hints.en: Determine the minimum output value: Since the leading coefficient \( a = 1 > 0 \), the parabola opens upward, meaning that the vertex represents the absolute minimum point on the graph. The minimum value attained by \( f(x) \) is \(-4\).
hints.ar: حدّد minimum output value: Since the leading coefficient \( a = 1 > 0 \), the parabola opens upward, meaning that the vertex represents the absolute minimum point on the graph. The minimum value attained by \( f(x) \) is \(-4\).

hints.en: Determine the range: The range represents all possible output values (\(y\)-values) of the function. Because the function takes on its minimum value of \(-4\) at \(x = 1\) and increases without bound as \(x\) moves away from \(1\), the range is all real numbers greater than or equal to \(-4\), which is written in interval notation as \([-4, \infty)\).

solution.en:
1. **Identify the vertex and direction of opening**: The function \( f(x) = (x - 1)^2 - 4 \) is written in vertex form, \( f(x) = a(x - h)^2 + k \), where \( a = 1 \), \( h = 1 \), and \( k = -4 \). The vertex of the parabola is at \((1, -4)\).

2. **Determine the minimum output value**: Since the leading coefficient \( a = 1 > 0 \), the parabola opens upward, meaning that the vertex represents the absolute minimum point on the graph. The minimum value attained by \( f(x) \) is \(-4\).

3. **Determine the range**: The range represents all possible output values (\(y\)-values) of the function. Because the function takes on its minimum value of \(-4\) at \(x = 1\) and increases without bound as \(x\) moves away from \(1\), the range is all real numbers greater than or equal to \(-4\), which is written in interval notation as \([-4, \infty)\).

**Common Misconceptions:**
- Choice B, \([1, \infty)\), incorrectly uses the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex instead of the \(y\)-coordinate.
- Choice C, \((-\infty, -4]\), incorrectly assumes the parabola opens downward.
- Choice D, \((-\infty, \infty)\), confuses the range (the set of \(y\)-values) with the domain (the set of all real \(x\)-values).
